title: DC-area forecast: Scattered shower and storm odds increase late night into early Friday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Temperatures slowly dip back through the 80s on a humid evening. An isolated shower or storm may pass, especially southern parts of the area.

What’s next? Cooler highs in the upper 70s to mid-80s Friday into the weekend, with a few showers or storms possible this weekend.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: The chance of an isolated shower or storm continues during the evening, especially southern parts of the area. Scattered showers and storms become more likely overnight as we stay rather humid. Overnight lows in the upper 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): Isolated to scattered showers remain possible during the early morning hours, then skies should brighten some in the afternoon. It's cooler than today with highs in the upper 70s to mid-80s, although moderate humidity (dew points around the mid-60s) makes it feel less than ideal for September. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: Partly cloudy and still a bit humid with the chance of an isolated shower. Lows are again in the mid-60s to near 70. Confidence: Medium-High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

The weekend starts partly to mostly cloudy Saturday with highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. There could be a few showers or storms Saturday afternoon into the night. A little warmer Sunday with highs in the low to mid-80s. A couple showers and a storm could still be around, especially in eastern parts of the area. Confidence: Low-Medium

Mostly sunny Monday and Tuesday with upper 70s to mid-80s for highs. Perhaps a shot at 90 (maybe the last of the season?) in some spots by Wednesday. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 10

A sudden 2020 downpour set a rainfall record and triggered dangerous flash flooding, while in 1985 a prolonged late-season heat wave produced a record streak of 90-degree days.

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: Feeling like August with highs approaching 90, the heat index in the low to mid-90s, and an isolated shower or storm. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
